learning_objective: 🎯 Master describing words to make your sentences colourful, and learn how to compare things like a pro using the three degrees!

main_concepts.concept_title: ✨ Adjectives: The Color Palette of Grammar
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Adjectives are describing words that add flavour to nouns and pronouns. Instead of saying 'I saw a dog', you can use adjectives to say 'I saw a BIG, FLUFFY, BROWN dog'. They tell us what kind, which one, or how many!

This is the basic form of an adjective. You use it when you are just describing ONE person or thing without comparing it to anyone else. Example: 'Rohan is TALL.' We are just stating a fact about Rohan.

Use this when comparing exactly TWO things or people. We usually add '-er' to the adjective or put 'more' before it. We also use the word 'than'. Example: 'Rohan is TALLER than Amit' or 'This book is MORE EXCITING than that one.'

Use this when comparing THREE or MORE things to show who is the ultimate winner! We add '-est' or put 'most' before the adjective. Always remember to use 'The' before a superlative! Example: 'Rohan is THE TALLEST boy in the class.'

Some adjectives do not follow the '-er' or '-est' rules at all. They totally change their spelling! The most common ones are: Good - Better - Best, and Bad - Worse - Worst. You just have to memorize these rule breakers!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Family Comparison Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Look at your family members. Write three sentences using degrees of comparison! Example: 'My sister is SHORT (Positive). I am SHORTER than my sister (Comparative). My little brother is the SHORTEST in the family (Superlative).'

quick_recap: ⭐ Adjectives describe or modify nouns and pronouns.
⭐ Comparative degree compares two things, usually ending in -er (Faster).
⭐ Superlative degree compares three or more things, usually ending in -est (Fastest).
⭐ Long adjectives use 'more' and 'most' instead of -er and -est (Beautiful -> More beautiful).
